chords._schema: strings ordered low E (6) to high e (1). frets: null = muted/not played, 0 = open. fingers: 0 = open, 1 = index, 2 = middle, 3 = ring, 4 = pinky, null = muted.

exercises.name: Make the D shape
exercises.purpose: Land the bright D chord that completes the I-IV-V.

params.fingers: middle(2) on G 2nd fret, ring(3) on B 3rd fret, pinky(4) on high-e 2nd fret, low E and A muted
params.strings_played: D, G, B, high e (low E and A stay quiet)

exercises.coaching: D is the third colour. Middle on the G, second fret; ring on the B, third fret; pinky on the high e, second fret; keep the low E and A quiet. That tight little shape is the D chord — punchy and bright.

exercises.name: The I-IV-V turnaround
exercises.purpose: Practice G to C to D — the classic country progression.

params.cue: one chord per 4 beats, change on the downbeat

exercises.coaching: Walk the turnaround: G, C, D — one per four beats. Slow it right down so every change lands on the click. D is the bright tension that wants to fall back to G. That pull is the whole story of country.

exercises.name: Your first I-IV-V loop
exercises.purpose: Play the full G-C-D-G loop top to bottom.

params.cue: one chord per bar, change on bar 1; loop it

exercises.coaching: Here it is — the I-IV-V. G for four beats, C for four, D for four, back to G. One chord per bar, on the click. Slow is fine. You are playing the progression behind a century of country. Loop it. That is country.

avatar_coaching_copy.intro: The payoff lesson. Three chords — G, C, D — and you can play a full I-IV-V. This is the progression behind a hundred years of country.
avatar_coaching_copy.ex1_intro: D is the triangle: middle on G second, ring on B third, pinky on high e second, low E and A quiet. The open D string is your root — that punch is the sound.
avatar_coaching_copy.ex2_intro: Walk the turnaround: G, C, D, one per four beats, slow. D is the tension that wants to fall back to G. That pull is the whole story.
avatar_coaching_copy.ex3_intro: The I-IV-V: G four beats, C four, D four, back to G. One chord per bar, on the click. Slow is fine. Loop it. That is country.
avatar_coaching_copy.results: If you can play the I-IV-V without stopping, you have the backbone of the entire style. Loop it every practice — it never gets old.
avatar_coaching_copy.wrap: G, C, D — a full I-IV-V in your hands. That is the Country style pack. Play it with the boom-chick, play it with feeling, and you are a country player.
